destination.title: Police Came for a Welfare Check and Left With His Guns — No Warrant

short53: His wife asked the police to check
They left his house carrying his guns.
a handgun set on the dining table
his wife sleeps at a hotel.
By morning she can't reach him.
He agrees to a psychiatric evaluation on one condition he says:
they walk into his home no warrant no emergency
They called it caretaking. For years
So he carried one question to the Supreme Court:
can police enter your home just to
Caretaking does not open your front door.
Follow for the cases they don't teach you

candidate_payload_lines: It called the police work "community caretaking functions", the routine, non-criminal business of clearing wrecks and securing hazards, "totally divorced" from investigating a crime.
So how did her phone call end with officers inside his house, his handguns in an evidence bag, no warrant, and no crime?
Can the police come into your home, without a warrant, simply to look after you?
It is August 2015, in a house in Cranston, and a marriage is under strain.
So she calls the Cranston police, not 911, the non-emergency line, and asks them to do a welfare check.
Whether they can cross your threshold without a warrant for the gentlest reason there is, to look after you, and carry out what they find.
From a single Supreme Court case in 1973: Cady versus Dombrowski.
They heard argument on the twenty-fourth of March, 2021.
There is no free-standing community-caretaking exception that lets the police enter your home without a warrant.
The Court did not say the police can never enter your home without a warrant.
The Chief Justice, joined by Justice Breyer, stressed that no warrant is needed to help a person who is seriously injured or threatened with injury.
Whether the police can enter your home, without a warrant, simply to look after you, and take what they find.
After May 2021, the caretaking version of that excuse is gone.

And there is a harder one still: when the person the police fear for is not a stranger on a highway but a neighbor they believe is about to end their own life, no one has yet settled how much they may do, or for how long.
If you started this thinking a welfare check could never reach past your own front door, and you see the line differently now, that is worth a like.
